newsitem.title: GERMANY: German officials agree to cull British, Swiss cows.
newsitem.headline: German officials agree to cull British, Swiss cows.

text.p: German officials agreed on Wednesday to slaughter around 5,200 cattle imported from Britain and Switzerland after fears sparked by a fresh case of mad cow disease in Germany.

The officials from the federal government and Germany's 16 regional states also agreed to put the 14,000 offspring of Swiss and British cattle under strict observation while they investigated the latest case.

The decision would affect around 2,600 animals imported from Britain and around the same number from Switzerland, agriculture ministry state secretary Franz-Josef Feiter told a news conference in Bonn.
He said around 12,000 cattle of British origin and 2,000 from Swiss stock would be placed under observation. Switzerland has recorded the highest number of cases of BSE after Britain.
"The consumer must be able to be sure that he can buy meat here without the risk of BSE," Feiter said.
The officials agreed the measures after the agriculture ministry said on Tuesday one German-born cow had died from bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) or mad cow disease.
The case appeared to be a first as Germany's four previous cases of BSE had all involved animals imported from Britain.
But Feiter said the origin of the cow in question, which died last December, was far from clear.
There was some doubt over the cow's ear-tag, making it possible the animal may been imported from Britain rather than born in Germany to a British mother, Feiter said.
The animal's presumed mother had now been traced he added. She was sold to a farm in the Netherlands, where she had another calf and was slaughtered last year without any suspicion of BSE.
"This would be the first case of possible infection from mother to calf," Feiter said. "Such a case has not even come to light in Britain."
